messages:
Maya: Heads up — we're seeing a hosted API p99 spike starting ~2026-03-18 11:12 UTC. p99 ~1.8s (was ~220ms), p95 up to ~600ms. Dash: https://internal.redwood/dash/hosted/p99 . Kernel-selector v2 rolled at ~10:50 UTC (small canary then ramp). Queue depth on affected shards jumped to ~250-350.
Chris: looking. grabbing flame and trace from the 11:12 window now.
deploy-bot: rollout: kernel-selector-v2 -> 75% @ 2026-03-18T10:50:31Z (chris)
Samir: quick observation from kv-metrics: eviction-rate spikes aligned with the p99 spike window. evict/sec went from ~50 -> ~120. KV cache hit rate dropped ~12% for short-seq model. suspect priming churn.
Maya: interesting — metrics show batch-size median dropped from 12 -> 4 around same time. smaller batches + higher miss rate could explain cost per-token increase.
Chris: profiling snippet (11:12:30 - 11:14:30):
```
- scheduler coalesce wait: 7.2ms -> 1.9ms (more aggressive short-coalesce)
- kernel switch time (aux->main): 95ms median (cold code path)
- decoder startup (KV miss path): 110ms median
- per-request overhead increase correlated with <8 token KV prime responses
```
Chris: kernel-selector-v2 changed affinity heuristics to prefer aux kernels for short sequences; looks like combined with aggressive coalesce it created many tiny batches that hit the missy KV path frequently.
Katie: if tiny batches + kv miss = decoder startup cost, we can either relax coalescing or bias selector away from aux for tenants with heavy priming. Can we test bumping coalesce_window_ms from 4 -> 12 on affected pool?
Samir: I can toggle a debug flag to disable priming eviction for one minute on a single shard to validate. That should keep hit-rate stable and confirm hypothesis.
Ivan: proposed short mitigation plan:
- [now] route 20% of traffic away from kernel-selector-v2 to legacy selector for high-traffic tenants (config flip)
- [+10m] increase coalesce_window_ms on impacted queues to 12ms
- [+20m] enable kv eviction-sampling logs for 15m, capture full traces for 11:00-12:00
- [+30m] if p99 not improving, rollback kernel-selector-v2 to previous version
Maya: agree. Chris, can you run the route flip and coalesce change? Samir can do the eviction-sampling. I'll monitor dashboards.
Chris: doing route flip now -> flipped 20% traffic for hosted-prod pool A. coalesce_window_ms set to 12ms on that pool.
Samir: eviction-sampling enabled (shard s-42) for 15m; pushing full traces to s3://perf/priming-1768461200.tar
Maya: initial sign — p95 down to ~420ms on the canary pool, p99 trending down (was 1.8s -> 1.0s). queue depth on canary shards dropped ~60%.
Ivan: good signal. keep canary for 30m, then consider broader rollout of coalesce change + selector tweak.
Katie: follow-up action: add a regression test that simulates priming churn with kernel-selector variants + assert batch-size distribution doesn't collapse below N=6 for high-throughput tenants.
Maya: created ticket PERF-4823 and assigned to eng-runtime. I'll post summary in incidents once we confirm full resolution. :thumbsup:
Chris: will prepare rollback playbook in case of regression during ramp. :eyes:
